messages.content:
You are checking a research plan against a list of experimental controls. You are not asked whether the plan is good. For each control of the list you give two separate answers: CONTENT (does the plan state this control?) and PLACE (is the passage written under an experiment that it can check?).

PLAN. A sequence of actions written one after the other by a planner. Each action adds or revises one proposed experiment and usually has the fields ACTION, TITLE, PROPOSAL, CONTROLS, COST and PREDICTION. Actions are separated by blank lines and are given in the order they were written. Every action counts, including an action that revises an earlier one and an action that looks incomplete.

REFERENCE CONTROLS. A list of experimental controls. Each has an identifier and a description.

CONTENT. Give exactly one content status for each reference control. Judge the content only, wherever the passage is written in the plan.
- "conforme": a passage of the plan states what the description requires (what is compared, held fixed, varied, repeated, measured or excluded). Different wording is fine. Nothing essential is missing or weakened.
- "altere": a passage of the plan states a recognisable but partial, vaguer, reduced or modified version of the control.
- "absent": no passage of the plan states this control.
If the control is stated in several places, keep the best content status found (conforme, then altere, then absent) and quote the passage that earns it. If several passages earn the same best status, quote one whose PLACE is "checks" if there is one.

PLACE. Only for "conforme" and "altere". Read the action that contains your quote, and judge it against the experiment that this action proposes (its TITLE and PROPOSAL), not against the description of the reference control. If that action has no TITLE and no PROPOSAL, answer "general" if the quoted control is general, otherwise "cannot_check".
- "checks": this experiment is one whose result the quoted control would check.
- "cannot_check": this experiment has nothing for the quoted control to compare, hold fixed, vary, repeat, measure or exclude.
- "general": the quoted control names no model, dataset, metric, quantity, condition or comparison that belongs to one experiment; it would apply to any experiment of the plan.
For "absent", PLACE is null. Your PLACE answer must never change your CONTENT answer.

Rules.
1. Judge each reference control on its own. One passage may support several controls.
2. Judge only what is written. Do not credit a control because it would be sensible, usual or implied. Do not lower a status for style, length, order or cost.
3. Evidence. For "conforme" and "altere", quote the passage that carries the control. Copy it character for character from a single action: no ellipsis, no added or removed word, no corrected spelling, no changed punctuation, no paraphrase. Take the shortest passage that is enough: at least 24 characters, at most 300 characters; if the whole field that carries the control is shorter than 24 characters, quote the whole field. A program searches the plan for your quote, word for word; a quote that is not found counts as "absent".
4. For "absent", the quote is null.
5. Give an answer for every reference control, and for no other identifier.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, in this form:
{"<identifier>": {"content": "conforme" | "altere" | "absent", "quote": "<quote>" | null, "place": "checks" | "cannot_check" | "general" | null}, ...}

PLAN
<<<
ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of ablating the retrieval head on agreement with the reference labels for Halden-S
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Halden-S on the Drummer translation pairs and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after ablating the retrieval head. All runs share one data order for the Drummer translation pairs, so that differences in agreement with the reference labels cannot come from batching.
CONTROLS: (1) Match the number of training steps between Halden-S and Tessel-9. (2) Run Halden-S on the Drummer translation pairs with five random seeds and report the spread of agreement with the reference labels. (3) Ablate ablating the retrieval head alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on agreement with the reference labels.
COST: 31 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Agreement with the reference labels degrades on the Pryce reasoning chains while it holds on the Drummer translation pairs.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of halving the learning rate on mean token overlap for Marrow-3
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Marrow-3 on the Avenel retrieval pool and measure mean token overlap before and after halving the learning rate. We report mean token overlap separately for short and long inputs of the Avenel retrieval pool, since halving the learning rate may act differently on each. All runs share one data order for the Avenel retrieval pool, so that differences in mean token overlap cannot come from batching.
CONTROLS: (1) Match the number of training steps between Marrow-3 and Pelleas-4. (2) Include Pelleas-4 as a baseline under the same training budget. (3) Ablate halving the learning rate alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on mean token overlap.
COST: 8 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Mean token overlap degrades on the Wexcombe caption set while it holds on the Avenel retrieval pool.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of distilling into a 4-bit student on refusal rate for Ostrava-7
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ostrava-7 on the Halvard corpus and measure refusal rate before and after distilling into a 4-bit student. We plan one pilot run on a tenth of the Halvard corpus to check that refusal rate is not saturated before the full experiment. The analysis is restricted to the examples of the Halvard corpus that Ostrava-7 answers correctly before the intervention. We expect the effect of distilling into a 4-bit student to be smaller for Ilexa-6 than for Ostrava-7, because Ilexa-6 was never exposed to the Senna safety prompts.
CONTROLS: (1) Repeat the evaluation of refusal rate on the Halvard corpus with a second prompt template. (2) Shuffle the labels of the Halvard corpus as a negative control for refusal rate. (3) Include Ilexa-6 as a baseline under the same training budget.
COST: 26 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Refusal rate degrades on the Senna safety prompts while it holds on the Halvard corpus.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of adding label noise at 10% on calibration error for Quillon-L
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Quillon-L on the Tolwyn dialogue logs and measure calibration error before and after adding label noise at 10%. Each configuration of Quillon-L is trained for the same number of steps and evaluated at three checkpoints. A null result on calibration error would still be informative if area under the detection curve on the Brenna-QA set also stays within its usual range.
CONTROLS: (1) Report area under the detection curve on the Tolwyn dialogue logs to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric. (2) Report area under the detection curve on the Tolwyn dialogue logs to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric. (3) Repeat the evaluation of calibration error on the Tolwyn dialogue logs with a second prompt template.
COST: 27 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in calibration error beyond seed noise on the Tolwyn dialogue logs.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of removing the warm-up phase on exact-match accuracy for Varnok-2B
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Varnok-2B on the Lowick tabular benchmark and measure exact-match accuracy before and after removing the warm-up phase. We plan one pilot run on a tenth of the Lowick tabular benchmark to check that exact-match accuracy is not saturated before the full experiment. All runs share one data order for the Lowick tabular benchmark, so that differences in exact-match accuracy cannot come from batching.
CONTROLS: (1) Shuffle the labels of the Lowick tabular benchmark as a negative control for exact-match accuracy. (2) Shuffle the labels of the Lowick tabular benchmark as a negative control for exact-match accuracy. (3) Report false-alarm rate at fixed recall on the Lowick tabular benchmark to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric.
COST: 32 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Exact-match accuracy improves by a small but reliable margin on the Lowick tabular benchmark.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of ablating the retrieval head on agreement with the reference labels for Halden-S
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Halden-S on the Drummer translation pairs and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after ablating the retrieval head. We compare against Tessel-9, trained with the same budget on the Drummer translation pairs. We report agreement with the reference labels separately for short and long inputs of the Drummer translation pairs, since ablating the retrieval head may act differently on each.
CONTROLS: (1) Include Tessel-9 as a baseline under the same training budget. (2) Ablate ablating the retrieval head alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on agreement with the reference labels. (3) Shuffle the labels of the Drummer translation pairs as a negative control for agreement with the reference labels.
COST: 4 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in agreement with the reference labels beyond seed noise on the Drummer translation pairs.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of halving the learning rate on mean token overlap for Marrow-3
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Marrow-3 on the Avenel retrieval pool and measure mean token overlap before and after halving the learning rate. We also evaluate transfer to the Wexcombe caption set without further tuning of Marrow-3. All runs share one data order for the Avenel retrieval pool, so that differences in mean token overlap cannot come from batching. The analysis is restricted to the examples of the Avenel retrieval pool that Marrow-3 answers correctly before the intervention.
CONTROLS: (1) Include Pelleas-4 as a baseline under the same training budget. (2) Repeat the evaluation of mean token overlap on the Avenel retrieval pool with a second prompt template. (3) Run Marrow-3 on the Avenel retrieval pool with five random seeds and report the spread of mean token overlap.
COST: 36 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in mean token overlap beyond seed noise on the Avenel retrieval pool.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of distilling into a 4-bit student on refusal rate for Ostrava-7
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ostrava-7 on the Halvard corpus and measure refusal rate before and after distilling into a 4-bit student. A secondary readout is recall at 5, reported on the held-out split of the Halvard corpus. If refusal rate moves while recall at 5 stays flat, we attribute the change to distilling into a 4-bit student rather than to capacity. We compare against Ilexa-6, trained with the same budget on the Halvard corpus.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on the Senna safety prompts as a held-out distribution. (2) Ablate distilling into a 4-bit student alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on refusal rate. (3) Run Ostrava-7 on the Halvard corpus with five random seeds and report the spread of refusal rate.
COST: 37 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in refusal rate beyond seed noise on the Halvard corpus.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of adding label noise at 10% on calibration error for Quillon-L
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Quillon-L on the Tolwyn dialogue logs and measure calibration error before and after adding label noise at 10%. A secondary readout is area under the detection curve, reported on the held-out split of the Tolwyn dialogue logs. We expect the effect of adding label noise at 10% to be smaller for Corvane-12 than for Quillon-L, because Corvane-12 was never exposed to the Brenna-QA set.
CONTROLS: (1) Run Quillon-L on the Tolwyn dialogue logs with five random seeds and report the spread of calibration error. (2) Shuffle the labels of the Tolwyn dialogue logs as a negative control for calibration error. (3) Repeat the evaluation of calibration error on the Tolwyn dialogue logs with a second prompt template.
COST: 18 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Calibration error improves by a small but reliable margin on the Tolwyn dialogue logs.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of removing the warm-up phase on exact-match accuracy for Varnok-2B
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Varnok-2B on the Lowick tabular benchmark and measure exact-match accuracy before and after removing the warm-up phase. We compare against Sundrow-M, trained with the same budget on the Lowick tabular benchmark. Each configuration of Varnok-2B is trained for the same number of steps and evaluated at three checkpoints. We also evaluate transfer to the Kettering proofs without further tuning of Varnok-2B.
CONTROLS: (1) Match the number of training steps between Varnok-2B and Sundrow-M. (2) Repeat the evaluation of exact-match accuracy on the Lowick tabular benchmark with a second prompt template. (3) Ablate removing the warm-up phase alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on exact-match accuracy.
COST: 2 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in exact-match accuracy beyond seed noise on the Lowick tabular benchmark.
>>>

REFERENCE CONTROLS
- id: c1 | description: Use the Lowick tabular benchmark with shuffled labels as a negative control for exact-match accuracy.
- id: c2 | description: Report area under the detection curve on the Tolwyn dialogue logs as a second metric, so that a gain on a single metric is not over-read.
- id: c3 | description: Measure rank correlation with the gold ordering on the Marisol summaries again with a different prompt template.
